title: Best Bet Tracking App (2026)
verdict: The best bet tracking app in 2026 depends on where your bets are. If they are spread across US sportsbooks, Pikkit is the easiest complete record: free, automatic, verified. If they go through one account that routes to many venues, TerminalUp is the tracker by construction, because every fill is recorded with its venue and price as it happens. Juice Reel tracks the widest range of books and adds verified picks records; Betstamp pairs tracking with a serious odds screen.

Tracking matters for one reason: without the price you took and the price at close on every bet, you cannot tell an edge from a hot streak. Every app here is judged on whether it captures those two numbers without you typing them.

ranking.fit: Bettors who trade across venues and want the record to be a by-product of placing the bet.
ranking.lacks: A $10,000 minimum; it does not import bets you placed elsewhere.
ranking.note: Every order placed through TerminalUp is logged with venue, price and size at fill, across the sportsbooks, exchanges and prediction markets it routes to, so the ledger is complete and the price is the executed price, not a screenshot.

ranking.fit: Bettors on mainstream US sportsbooks who want a zero-effort verified record.
ranking.lacks: No odds screen and no execution; it records what you did elsewhere.
ranking.note: Free automatic syncing from US books; profit by sport, book and bet type; social features.

ranking.fit: Bettors who use many books and DFS sites and want CLV tracked alongside verified picks records.
ranking.lacks: The picks marketplace and AI features add clutter if all you want is a log.
ranking.note: Syncs from hundreds of sportsbooks and DFS apps, tracks CLV and EV, verifies handicappers from their synced accounts.

ranking.fit: Bettors who want tracking and a deep odds screen in one place.
ranking.lacks: Less automatic than the sync-first apps on some books.
ranking.note: Free tracker with line shopping; PRO extends the screen to hundreds of books.

ranking.fit: Bettors who want tracking inside a content and public-betting-data app.
ranking.lacks: The tracker is secondary to the media product.
ranking.note: Action Network syncs bets from supported books and shows them next to its odds and betting-percentage data.

why: A tracker that imports bets from a book records the price the book reported. A terminal that places the bet records the price it actually filled at, on whichever venue had the best number, with the size and the time. For a bettor who moves between sportsbooks, exchanges and prediction markets, that is the only way the record stays complete: there is one account, every order goes through it, and nothing is placed off the ledger.

That also makes closing line value a native number rather than a reconstruction. The board that showed the best price at the time of the bet shows the closing prices too. TerminalUp charges 0.5% commission per trade (0.35% at the highest volume), no subscription, and never takes a position. You fund one TerminalUp account. Orders route to venues from it.
For bets placed outside it, Pikkit is the recommendation: free, automatic and honest about what it is.

faq.q: What is the best free bet tracker?
faq.a: Pikkit for US sportsbooks: automatic syncing, verified results, no cost. Betstamp and Juice Reel also have free tiers.

faq.q: Do bet tracking apps track closing line value?
faq.a: Juice Reel and Betstamp do for synced bets. TerminalUp records the executed price and the close across the venues it routes to.

faq.q: Can I track prediction market positions?
faq.a: Most sportsbook trackers do not sync Kalshi or Polymarket. TerminalUp logs orders it routes to prediction markets alongside sportsbook and exchange fills.
Because results over a few hundred bets are mostly variance. The price you took versus the closing price is the measure that separates skill from luck, and you need it on every bet.
It works if you record the closing price every time. Most people stop after a month, which is why automatic capture wins.

faq.q: Does TerminalUp import bets from other books?
faq.a: No. It records what is placed through it. For bets elsewhere, use Pikkit or Juice Reel.
